description: Pay transparency laws are rapidly expanding, with most U.S. job postings now including salary ranges. But regulators rarely define how wide those ranges can be, leaving employers broad discretion. Analyzing nearly 10 million postings researchers find that women disproportionately avoid jobs with wide ranges, driven partly by greater aversion to financial uncertainty. Women then negotiate less aggressively and accept lower starting pay, reinforcing existing gender wage gaps. However, the study also found that pairing ranges with simple contextual statements about how salary offers are determined substantially reduces these effects. To make sure all top talent applies to your post, leaders need to treat pay ranges as strategic signals, not compliance signals.
title: Research: Posting a Wide Salary Range Can Deter Women from Applying
